root_cause.finding: opal-data-cottonwood's BUCKET POLICY statement DenyForeignFirmPrincipals denies s3:* to every principal whose ARN is not like role/*-cot-* or one of three named users (Andrew_Berman, Andrew_Berman_Console, Opal_Terminal). The Holdings function runs as arn:aws:iam::313476888478:role/irpt-holdings-role, which matches neither, so its first S3 read (begin() on the current index) is refused; publication.py wraps that into PublicationRefused('publication index unavailable'), snapshot.py into SnapshotUnavailable, entry.py maps SnapshotUnavailable to NOT_READY, and served.py refuses at :938 with the directory's business date.
root_cause.discriminator: aws iam simulate-principal-policy for irpt-holdings-role with --resource-policy = the live bucket policy: s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on .../platinum/holdings/current/manifest.json -> explicitDeny, MatchedStatements ResourcePolicy; the same simulation without the bucket policy -> allowed (positive control). Every offline replay passed because the CTO's and M's credentials are the named users on the allow-list.
root_cause.why_prior_readbacks_missed_it: HOLDINGS_READER_CTO_LIVE_READBACK (22:13Z) and comp-iam simulate read the ROLE's identity policy; neither reads the bucket's resource policy. Rule 22: a check scoped to the members cannot see a defect in what the members share; the bucket policy is the shared dependency.

sibling_buckets.opal-data-49financial: same Deny; its ArnNotLike list already names 14 non-firm roles by exact ARN (the precedent shape)
sibling_buckets.opal-data-inflection: same Deny; wildcard role/*-inf-* plus the three users only

root_cause.consequence: irpt-holdings is denied on all three firm buckets today; the 49F and INF Holdings publications would be unreadable by the function the same way once published.

remedy.shape: add the exact ARN arn:aws:iam::313476888478:role/irpt-holdings-role to the DenyForeignFirmPrincipals ArnNotLike list on opal-data-cottonwood, opal-data-49financial and opal-data-inflection, in the Terraform root that owns those bucket policies (never a console edit); the reader's own identity policy stays prefix-scoped and firm-bound in code, so the cross-firm guard's intent holds: a shared reader is admitted by NAME, never by wildcard
